sentence_stem: After the long journey, he stopped
correct_completion: to buy some water at the station.
full_sentence: After the long journey, he stopped to buy some water at the station.
acceptable_variants: to get some water at the station.

options.text: buying some water at the station.
options.why_wrong: 'Stop + gerund' means he ended an activity. Here the sentence needs a purpose, so 'stop + infinitive' is required.

options.text: to buy some water at the station.
buy some water at the station.
options.why_wrong: A bare infinitive without 'to' cannot follow 'stopped' in this structure.
'Having bought' describes a completed action before the stop, so it does not explain why he stopped.

grammar_focus: Stop + infinitive of purpose versus stop + gerund
explanation: After 'stopped', an infinitive with 'to' shows the purpose of stopping, while a gerund shows that an activity was ended. Turkish speakers often rely on a purpose suffix in their own language, so they may need to think about the verb pattern in English more explicitly.
